claim: Since November 15, 2023 an instance maintenance policy lets you choose whether replacement instances launch before or after existing instances are terminated, for events such as an instance refresh or a health check replacement.
question: Since when can you make Auto Scaling launch a replacement before it terminates an unhealthy instance?

values.display: launched before or after existing instances are terminated

evidence.quote: You can configure an instance maintenance policy for your Auto Scaling group to meet specific capacity requirements during events that cause instances to be replaced, such as an instance refresh or the health check process.
With an instance maintenance policy, you can make sure that Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling first launches a new instance and then waits for it to be fully ready before terminating the unhealthy instance.

| [Instance maintenance policies](#DocumentHistory) | You can now use an instance maintenance policy to define whether instances are launched before or after existing instances are terminated during events that cause your instances to be replaced, including an instance refresh. For more information, see [Instance maintenance policies](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/ec2-auto-scaling-instance-maintenance-policy.html) in the *Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling User Guide*. | November 15, 2023 |

claim: The price-capacity-optimized Spot allocation strategy was added on November 10, 2022; it requests Spot Instances from the pools least likely to be interrupted that also have the lowest possible price, and AWS now recommends it when you are getting started.
question: When was the price-capacity-optimized Spot allocation strategy added, and what does it choose?

values.display: price and capacity optimized allocation strategy

evidence.quote: We recommend this strategy when you're getting started.

| [New Spot allocation strategy](#DocumentHistory) | You can now use the price and capacity optimized allocation strategy to request Spot Instances from the Spot pools that are the least likely to be interrupted and have the lowest possible price. For more information, see [Allocation strategies](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/ec2-auto-scaling-mixed-instances-groups.html#allocation-strategies) in the *Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling User Guide*. | November 10, 2022 |

note: Change since mid-2022 (FRESHNESS: Spot allocation guidance). Current-truth: ec2-auto-scaling-spot-price-capacity-optimized-recommended and ec2-auto-scaling-spot-lowest-price-not-recommended. Older questions may treat lowest-price or capacity-optimized as the best answer. Evidence 0 'this strategy' is the price-capacity-optimized entry (line above it on the page).

claim: Since January 19, 2023 a launch template for an Auto Scaling group can name a Systems Manager parameter instead of an AMI ID, so the group can use new AMI IDs without new launch templates or versions.
question: Since when can an Auto Scaling launch template reference a Systems Manager parameter instead of an AMI ID?

values.display: Systems Manager parameter instead of an AMI ID

evidence.quote: With Systems Manager parameters, you can update your Auto Scaling groups to use new AMI IDs without needing to create new launch templates or new versions of launch templates each time an AMI ID changes.

| [Support for using an AWS Systems Manager parameter for an AMI ID](#DocumentHistory) | You can now use a Systems Manager parameter instead of an AMI ID in your launch template. For more information, see [Using AWS Systems Manager parameters instead of AMI IDs in launch templates](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/using-systems-manager-parameters.html) in the *Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling User Guide*. | January 19, 2023 |

claim: On February 10, 2023 instance refresh gained rollback of changes from a failed refresh, and the choice to terminate or ignore standby instances and to replace or ignore scale-in protected instances instead of waiting for them.
question: When did instance refresh gain rollback and handling of standby and scale-in protected instances?

values.display: roll back changes from a failed instance refresh

evidence.quote: | [New instance refresh features](#DocumentHistory) | You can now choose to terminate or ignore instances on standby and replace or ignore instances protected from scale in, instead of waiting for them to become replaceable. You can also roll back changes from a failed instance refresh. As part of this update, the documentation has been expanded to include topics for rolling back an instance refresh, cancelling an instance refresh, and understanding the default values for the configurable parameters of an instance refresh. For more information, see [Replacing Auto Scaling instances based on an instance refresh](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/asg-instance-refresh.html) in the *Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling User Guide*. | February 10, 2023 |

note: Change since mid-2022. Alarm-based rollback followed on July 31, 2023 (ec2-auto-scaling-change-instance-refresh-alarm-rollback-2023).

claim: If an Auto Scaling group uses a launch template that specifies a Systems Manager parameter for the AMI, warm pools are not supported, and you cannot start an instance refresh with a desired configuration or skip matching.
question: Which features are not available when the launch template uses a Systems Manager parameter for the AMI?

qualifiers.condition: launch template specifies a Systems Manager parameter

evidence.quote: If your Auto Scaling group uses a launch template that specifies a Systems Manager parameter, warm pools are not supported.
If your Auto Scaling group uses a launch template that specifies a Systems Manager parameter, you will not be able to start an instance refresh with a desired configuration or using skip matching.

note: Decision: SSM parameter vs warm pool.

claim: Auto Scaling resolves the Systems Manager parameter on each create or update call for the group; with advanced parameters or higher throughput limits, these GetParameters calls can raise Systems Manager cost, which is charged per Parameter Store API interaction.
question: What extra cost can a Systems Manager AMI parameter in a launch template cause?

values.display: charges are incurred per Parameter Store API interaction

qualifiers.condition: advanced parameters or higher throughput limits

evidence.quote: On each call to create or update your Auto Scaling group, Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling will resolve the Systems Manager parameter in the launch template.

If you are using advanced parameters or higher throughput limits, the frequent calls to the Parameter Store (that is, the `GetParameters` operation) can increase your costs for Systems Manager because charges are incurred per Parameter Store API interaction.

claim: To specify a Parameter Store parameter in a launch template you need ssm:GetParameters on that parameter, and anyone who uses the launch template also needs it so the value can be validated.
question: Which IAM permission is needed to use a launch template that references a Systems Manager parameter?

evidence.quote: To specify a parameter from the Parameter Store in a launch template, you must have the `ssm:GetParameters` permission for the specified parameter.
Anyone who uses the launch template also needs the `ssm:GetParameters` permission in order for the parameter value to be validated.

claim: When a group uses the $Latest or $Default launch template version, later launches use the service-linked role's permissions, so a user who can update the template could pass an IAM role to instances without iam:PassRole; the autoscaling:LaunchTemplateVersionSpecified condition key limits this.
question: What security risk comes from letting a group use the $Latest or $Default launch template version, and which condition key limits it?

values.display: even if they don't have the `iam:PassRole` permission

evidence.quote: This means that a user who is using the launch template could potentially update it to pass an IAM role to an instance even if they don't have the `iam:PassRole` permission.
Use the `autoscaling:LaunchTemplateVersionSpecified` condition key if you want to limit who has access to configuring groups to use the `$Latest` or `$Default` version.
